classification.difficultyReason: Convert mixed length units before applying the triangle-area formula, including an external perpendicular height and a rotated right triangle.

content.prompt: Calculate the area of these shapes. Give your answer in the smaller unit.

spec.description: Triangle with a base sloping downwards to the right, an internal dashed perpendicular altitude and a right-angle marker at its foot.
spec.mathematics: Base 0.8 m; perpendicular height 25 cm. The altitude foot is obtained by perpendicular projection onto the base. Drawing coordinates preserve the source orientation and are not additional measurements.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied dimensions and marks appear; the supplied area is excluded.

spec.description: Narrow obtuse triangle with a horizontal base. A separate dashed vertical height indicator stands to the left, with a top cap, rotated height label and a right-angle marker at the lower baseline. A visible gap separates that baseline segment from the triangle's base.
spec.mathematics: Base 0.22 m; external perpendicular height 58 cm. The height indicator spans the vertical distance from the base level to the upper vertex level.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied dimensions and marks appear; the supplied area is excluded.

spec.description: Rotated right triangle with the right angle at its upper vertex. The left leg is labelled 1.6 cm, the right leg 43 mm, and the lower hypotenuse is unlabelled.
spec.mathematics: The labelled legs are perpendicular and supply the base and height. Coordinates enforce the marked right angle while retaining the source's schematic orientation.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied dimensions and marks appear; the supplied area is excluded.

answer.worked:
$1.6\,\text{cm}=16\,\text{mm}$. The two labelled sides are perpendicular.
$$\begin{align*} A &= \frac{bh}{2} \\ A &= \frac{16(43)}{2} \\ A &= 344\,\text{mm}^2 \end{align*}$$
